paragraphs.title: Family Honor and the Prohibition of Incest

easy.question: What is a man forbidden to do according to the verse?
answers: Take his father's wife
Take his sister
Take his daughter
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “A man shall not take his father's wife.”

easy.question: What else is forbidden according to the verse?
answers: Uncover his father's face
Uncover his father's nakedness
Uncover his father's house
easy.explanation: The second part says, “He shall not uncover his father's nakedness.”

easy.question: Who is meant by the word “man” in the verse?
answers: The father
The woman
The male
easy.explanation: The word “man” refers to the male subject of the prohibition.

medium.question: What two prohibitions appear in the verse?
answers: Taking property and revealing a secret
Taking the father's wife and uncovering the father's nakedness
Leaving the father and harming him
medium.explanation: The verse contains both a prohibition against taking the father's wife and one against uncovering his nakedness.

medium.question: In the phrase “he shall not uncover his father's nakedness,” what does “nakedness” refer to?
answers: The edge or covering of a garment
Only a bird's wing
A house door
medium.explanation: In this context, the phrase refers figuratively to a person's covering, modesty, and marital dignity.

medium.question: What is the relationship between the two parts of the verse?
answers: The second part concerns an entirely different command
The second part permits what the first forbids
The second part reinforces and explains the seriousness of the first prohibition
medium.explanation: The two parts are related: taking the father's wife is also portrayed as violating the father's honor and marital rights.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the wording “his father's wife” rather than “his mother”?
answers: The prohibition concerns only his biological mother
The prohibition is unrelated to marriage
The prohibition includes the father's wife even if she is not the man's mother
challenge.explanation: “His father's wife” is broader than “his mother” and refers to the father's wife as such.

challenge.question: What possible symbolic meaning does “his father's nakedness” have in the verse?
answers: The personal space and honor connected with the father's marriage
An actual part of the father's body
The father's weapon
challenge.explanation: The phrase can symbolize covering, personal boundaries, and honor; uncovering it represents violating the father's status and marriage.

challenge.question: What detail in the structure of the verse is easy to miss?
answers: The verse commands taking the father's wife
The verse presents the prohibition both as an action and in symbolic language
The verse speaks only about a garment's covering
challenge.explanation: The prohibition appears both as the direct action “shall not take” and the symbolic expression “shall not uncover his father's nakedness.”

questions.question: What can be inferred from the wording “his father's wife” rather than “his mother”?
answers: The prohibition concerns only his biological mother
The prohibition is unrelated to marriage
The prohibition includes the father's wife even if she is not the man's mother
questions.explanation: “His father's wife” is broader than “his mother” and refers to the father's wife as such.

questions.question: What possible symbolic meaning does “his father's nakedness” have in the verse?
answers: The personal space and honor connected with the father's marriage
An actual part of the father's body
The father's weapon
questions.explanation: The phrase can symbolize covering, personal boundaries, and honor; uncovering it represents violating the father's status and marriage.

questions.question: What detail in the structure of the verse is easy to miss?
answers: The verse commands taking the father's wife
The verse presents the prohibition both as an action and in symbolic language
The verse speaks only about a garment's covering
questions.explanation: The prohibition appears both as the direct action “shall not take” and the symbolic expression “shall not uncover his father's nakedness.”

paragraphs.title: Boundaries of the Congregation and Belonging to It

easy.question: Who may not enter the congregation of the LORD according to verse 2?
answers: He who is wounded in the stones or has his privy member cut off
Every foreigner
Only the king of Israel
easy.explanation: Verse 2 explicitly says that such a man may not enter the congregation of the LORD.

easy.question: Who is mentioned in verse 3 as unable to enter the congregation of the LORD?
answers: The stranger
The bastard
The priest
easy.explanation: Verse 3 says, “A bastard shall not enter the congregation of the LORD.”

easy.question: To which generation does the verse say the bastard may not enter the congregation of the LORD?
answers: The third generation
The seventh generation
The tenth generation
easy.explanation: The verse emphasizes that even the tenth generation may not enter the congregation of the LORD.

medium.question: What do all the people mentioned in the two verses have in common?
answers: They are told not to enter the congregation of the LORD
They are told to go to war
They are told to bring an offering
medium.explanation: Both verses repeat the prohibition, “shall not enter the congregation of the LORD.”

medium.question: In the phrase “A bastard shall not enter the congregation of the LORD,” what does “bastard” mean?
answers: A public official
A person born from a forbidden relationship according to the Torah
A person from another country
medium.explanation: Here, “bastard” refers to someone born from a relationship forbidden by the Torah.

medium.question: What additional detail is stated specifically about the bastard?
answers: He may not enter the city
Only he may not enter the Temple
Even his tenth generation may not enter the congregation of the LORD
medium.explanation: The verse adds the words “even to his tenth generation.”

challenge.question: To whom does the phrase “even to his tenth generation” refer in verse 3?
answers: The bastard and his descendants
All the people of Israel
The priests only
challenge.explanation: The phrase follows the statement about the bastard and therefore refers to him and his descendants.

challenge.question: What can be learned from the repetition of “shall not enter” in the two verses?
answers: The prohibition is stated only once
The verses emphasize a prohibition concerning several different groups
The bastard may enter after a short time
challenge.explanation: The repeated wording connects the groups and stresses that each is barred from the congregation of the LORD.

challenge.question: What does “even” emphasize in “even to his tenth generation”?
answers: The prohibition applies only to the first generation
The prohibition ends in the second generation
The prohibition continues even as far as the tenth generation
challenge.explanation: “Even” emphasizes that the restriction extends to the tenth generation, not merely to the person himself or his immediate descendants.

questions.question: To whom does the phrase “even to his tenth generation” refer in verse 3?
answers: The bastard and his descendants
All the people of Israel
The priests only
questions.explanation: The phrase follows the statement about the bastard and therefore refers to him and his descendants.

questions.question: What can be learned from the repetition of “shall not enter” in the two verses?
answers: The prohibition is stated only once
The verses emphasize a prohibition concerning several different groups
The bastard may enter after a short time
questions.explanation: The repeated wording connects the groups and stresses that each is barred from the congregation of the LORD.

questions.question: What does “even” emphasize in “even to his tenth generation”?
answers: The prohibition applies only to the first generation
The prohibition ends in the second generation
The prohibition continues even as far as the tenth generation
questions.explanation: “Even” emphasizes that the restriction extends to the tenth generation, not merely to the person himself or his immediate descendants.

paragraphs.title: Treatment of Ammon and Moab and the Memory of Balaam

easy.question: Which two nations may not enter the congregation of the LORD?
answers: Ammon and Moab
Egypt and Edom
Philistia and Canaan
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter the congregation of the LORD.”

easy.question: What did Ammon and Moab not provide for Israel on the way out of Egypt?
answers: Clothing and tools
Bread and water
Gold and silver
easy.explanation: The verse says that they did not meet Israel with bread and water.

easy.question: What did the LORD do to the curse Balaam wanted to pronounce on Israel?
answers: He returned it to Balaam
He merely canceled it
He turned it into a blessing
easy.explanation: The verse says that the LORD turned the curse into a blessing.

medium.question: Why were Ammon and Moab forbidden to enter the congregation of the LORD?
answers: Because they had served in Egypt
Because they did not help Israel and hired Balaam to curse them
Because they lived far from the land of Israel
medium.explanation: The verses mention both their failure to provide bread and water and their hiring Balaam to curse Israel.

medium.question: In the phrase “they met you not with bread and water,” what does “met” mean?
answers: Welcomed you with assistance and supplies
Went ahead of you to war
Arrived before you in the land
medium.explanation: In the context of bread and water, “met” means welcomed the travelers and supplied their needs.

medium.question: What did Balaam want to do, and what did the LORD actually do?
answers: Balaam wanted to bless Israel, and the LORD stopped him
Balaam wanted to curse Israel, and the LORD turned the curse into a blessing
Balaam wanted to fight, and the LORD made peace
medium.explanation: Ammon and Moab hired Balaam to curse Israel, but the LORD turned the curse into a blessing.

challenge.question: What meaning is emphasized by “even to their tenth generation” and “for ever”?
answers: The prohibition applies only to the first generation
The prohibition ends after ten generations
The prohibition is described as continuing without a time limit
challenge.explanation: Together, these expressions stress that the prohibition is not limited to ten generations.

challenge.question: What is the correct order of events in the verses?
answers: Ammon and Moab failed to help Israel, hired Balaam, and the LORD turned the curse into a blessing
The LORD blessed Israel, then Balaam was hired, and finally water was given to Israel
Balaam blessed Israel, then Ammon and Moab helped, and the LORD barred them
challenge.explanation: The verses first describe their failure to help, then the hiring of Balaam, and finally the LORD's turning the curse into a blessing.

challenge.question: What special instruction is given to Israel at the end of the passage?
answers: To seek the peace of Ammon and Moab
Never to seek their peace or prosperity
To offer Balaam peace and prosperity
challenge.explanation: The passage says, “Thou shalt not seek their peace nor their prosperity all thy days for ever.”

questions.question: What meaning is emphasized by “even to their tenth generation” and “for ever”?
answers: The prohibition applies only to the first generation
The prohibition ends after ten generations
The prohibition is described as continuing without a time limit
questions.explanation: Together, these expressions stress that the prohibition is not limited to ten generations.

questions.question: What is the correct order of events in the verses?
answers: Ammon and Moab failed to help Israel, hired Balaam, and the LORD turned the curse into a blessing
The LORD blessed Israel, then Balaam was hired, and finally water was given to Israel
Balaam blessed Israel, then Ammon and Moab helped, and the LORD barred them
questions.explanation: The verses first describe their failure to help, then the hiring of Balaam, and finally the LORD's turning the curse into a blessing.

questions.question: What special instruction is given to Israel at the end of the passage?
answers: To seek the peace of Ammon and Moab
Never to seek their peace or prosperity
To offer Balaam peace and prosperity
questions.explanation: The passage says, “Thou shalt not seek their peace nor their prosperity all thy days for ever.”

paragraphs.title: Treatment of Edomites and Egyptians and Acceptance in the Third Generation

easy.question: Whom must the Israelites not abhor?
answers: The Edomite
The Babylonian
The Canaanite
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite.”

easy.question: Why must the Israelites not abhor the Egyptian?
answers: Because the Egyptians were neighbors
Because Israel had been strangers in their land
Because the Egyptians were their brothers
easy.explanation: The verse explains, “Because thou wast a stranger in his land.”

easy.question: When may the descendants of the Edomite and Egyptian enter the congregation of the LORD?
answers: Immediately
In the first generation
In the third generation
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The children ... shall enter ... in their third generation.”

medium.question: What is the connection between the reasons for not abhorring the Edomite and the Egyptian?
answers: The Edomite is related as a brother, while Israel had once lived as strangers in Egypt
Both were enemies of Israel
Both helped Israel in the wilderness
medium.explanation: The Edomite is called a brother, while Egypt is remembered because Israel had lived there as strangers.

medium.question: What does “abhor” mean in “Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite”?
answers: Invite
Hate or reject
Bless
medium.explanation: “Abhor” means to hate or reject; the command forbids treating the Edomite with hatred.

medium.question: What is the order of the statements in the verses?
answers: The third generation is mentioned first, followed by the reasons
The Egyptians are mentioned first, followed by the Edomites
The prohibition against abhorring the Edomite and Egyptian comes first, followed by the rule about their descendants
medium.explanation: Verse 8 discusses the Edomite and Egyptian, and verse 9 states the condition concerning the third generation.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between the treatment of the Edomite and Egyptian and the rule about entering the congregation?
answers: They must not be hated now, but their descendants enter only in the third generation
They may be hated until the third generation
Only Egyptians may enter immediately
challenge.explanation: The prohibition against hatred applies immediately, while entry for their descendants is delayed until the third generation.

challenge.question: What special reason is given for the Egyptian but not for the Edomite?
answers: That the Egyptian is a relative
That Israel had been strangers in Egypt's land
That the Egyptian was in the wilderness with Israel
challenge.explanation: The Edomite is called a brother, but Israel's former residence in Egypt is given as the reason concerning the Egyptian.

challenge.question: What detail in verse 9 is easy to miss?
answers: The verse speaks only about Edomites
The verse says entry will occur in the second generation
The verse says that the descendants may enter only in the third generation
challenge.explanation: The word “third” means that entry is not permitted in the first or second generation.

questions.question: What is the main difference between the treatment of the Edomite and Egyptian and the rule about entering the congregation?
answers: They must not be hated now, but their descendants enter only in the third generation
They may be hated until the third generation
Only Egyptians may enter immediately
questions.explanation: The prohibition against hatred applies immediately, while entry for their descendants is delayed until the third generation.

questions.question: What special reason is given for the Egyptian but not for the Edomite?
answers: That the Egyptian is a relative
That Israel had been strangers in Egypt's land
That the Egyptian was in the wilderness with Israel
questions.explanation: The Edomite is called a brother, but Israel's former residence in Egypt is given as the reason concerning the Egyptian.

questions.question: What detail in verse 9 is easy to miss?
answers: The verse speaks only about Edomites
The verse says entry will occur in the second generation
The verse says that the descendants may enter only in the third generation
questions.explanation: The word “third” means that entry is not permitted in the first or second generation.

paragraphs.title: The Holiness and Purity of the Camp

easy.question: What must the camp guard against when it goes to war?
answers: Every wicked thing
Heavy rain
A shortage of water
easy.explanation: The verse commands, “Keep thee from every wicked thing.”

easy.question: Where must a man go if he is unclean because of a nocturnal emission?
answers: To the center of the camp
Outside the camp
To the commander's tent
easy.explanation: He must go outside the camp and may not immediately enter it.

easy.question: What is the paddle outside the camp used for?
answers: Hanging clothes
Marking the camp's boundary
Digging and covering excrement
easy.explanation: The verse commands him to dig with it and cover what comes from him.

medium.question: What is the order of actions for a man who leaves the camp because of a nocturnal emission?
answers: He enters immediately and washes afterward
He washes in the evening and enters after sunset
He remains outside the camp for three days
medium.explanation: First he washes with water in the evening; after sunset he may return to the camp.

medium.question: In this passage, what is a “nocturnal emission”?
answers: A frightening dream
A disease that occurs at night
The emission of semen during sleep
medium.explanation: The expression describes a bodily occurrence during sleep that requires the man to leave the camp and wash.

medium.question: Why must the camp be guarded and kept clean?
answers: Because the LORD walks in its midst
So the soldiers can sleep longer
So they do not lose their weapons
medium.explanation: The passage says that the LORD walks in the camp, so it must be holy and clean.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the commands both to cover excrement and to guard against every wicked thing?
answers: The command concerns only bodily cleanliness
The camp's holiness includes cleanliness and proper conduct
There is no need to maintain order in the camp
challenge.explanation: The verses connect practical cleanliness with avoiding wickedness as part of the camp's holiness.

challenge.question: What may happen if the camp is not holy and clean, according to the end of the passage?
answers: The LORD may turn away from behind the camp
The battle will begin immediately
The camp will move elsewhere
challenge.explanation: The passage warns that the LORD may see an unclean thing and turn away from the camp.

challenge.question: What does “every wicked thing” at the beginning of the passage teach?
answers: The prohibition applies only to the unclean man
The instructions apply only in peacetime
The requirement is broad and includes every wicked thing
challenge.explanation: The word “every” shows that the command is not limited to impurity or excrement but extends to all wickedness.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the commands both to cover excrement and to guard against every wicked thing?
answers: The command concerns only bodily cleanliness
The camp's holiness includes cleanliness and proper conduct
There is no need to maintain order in the camp
questions.explanation: The verses connect practical cleanliness with avoiding wickedness as part of the camp's holiness.

questions.question: What may happen if the camp is not holy and clean, according to the end of the passage?
answers: The LORD may turn away from behind the camp
The battle will begin immediately
The camp will move elsewhere
questions.explanation: The passage warns that the LORD may see an unclean thing and turn away from the camp.

questions.question: What does “every wicked thing” at the beginning of the passage teach?
answers: The prohibition applies only to the unclean man
The instructions apply only in peacetime
The requirement is broad and includes every wicked thing
questions.explanation: The word “every” shows that the command is not limited to impurity or excrement but extends to all wickedness.

easy.question: What must not be done to a servant who escapes from his master to you?
answers: He must not be delivered back to his master
He must not be given food
He must not be asked his name
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thou shalt not deliver unto his master the servant.”

easy.question: Where may the servant live?
answers: Only outside the city
Wherever he chooses in one of Israel's gates
Only in his former master's house
easy.explanation: He may dwell among Israel in the place he chooses at one of the gates.

easy.question: How must the servant not be treated?
answers: He must not be taught
He must not be allowed to choose a place
He must not be oppressed
easy.explanation: The verse concludes, “Thou shalt not oppress him.”

medium.question: What does “thou shalt not oppress him” mean?
answers: Do not oppress or mistreat him
Do not invite him to eat
Do not ask him to work
medium.explanation: The command means that he must not be oppressed, mistreated, or harmed.

medium.question: Why does the Torah command that the servant not be handed over?
answers: Because he must become king
Because he escaped his master and sought a safe place
Because servants may not leave the city
medium.explanation: The passage describes a servant who escaped and came for protection, so he must not be returned.

medium.question: Which sequence matches the commands in the verses?
answers: Return him to his master, then choose a gate for him
Punish him, then give him work
Do not deliver him, let him choose a place, and do not oppress him
medium.explanation: The verses first forbid returning him, then allow him to choose where to live, and finally forbid oppression.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “in the place which he shall choose”?
answers: The servant must live where his master decides
The servant may choose his own place of residence
The servant must move from place to place
challenge.explanation: The wording gives the escaped servant freedom to choose a suitable place to live.

challenge.question: What does “he shall dwell with thee, even among you” teach about society's treatment of the escaped servant?
answers: He may live within the community rather than merely hide outside it
He must be returned immediately to his master
People are forbidden to speak with him
challenge.explanation: The wording points to acceptance and protection within the community, not merely temporary shelter.

challenge.question: What detail limits the command not to deliver him?
answers: It applies only to a servant who chose a particular gate
It applies only to a servant who worked for a long time
It concerns a servant who escaped from his master and came to you
challenge.explanation: The passage concerns specifically a servant who escaped from his master and came to the Israelites.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “in the place which he shall choose”?
answers: The servant must live where his master decides
The servant may choose his own place of residence
The servant must move from place to place
questions.explanation: The wording gives the escaped servant freedom to choose a suitable place to live.

questions.question: What does “he shall dwell with thee, even among you” teach about society's treatment of the escaped servant?
answers: He may live within the community rather than merely hide outside it
He must be returned immediately to his master
People are forbidden to speak with him
questions.explanation: The wording points to acceptance and protection within the community, not merely temporary shelter.

questions.question: What detail limits the command not to deliver him?
answers: It applies only to a servant who chose a particular gate
It applies only to a servant who worked for a long time
It concerns a servant who escaped from his master and came to you
questions.explanation: The passage concerns specifically a servant who escaped from his master and came to the Israelites.

paragraphs.title: The Prohibition of Cultic Prostitution and the Dedication of Illicit Earnings

easy.question: What must not be found among the sons and daughters of Israel?
answers: A harlot or a sodomite
The poor and strangers
Kings and priests
easy.explanation: The verse says there shall be no whore among Israel's daughters or sodomite among Israel's sons.

easy.question: What must not be brought into the house of the LORD?
answers: Firstfruits
The hire of a whore or the price of a dog
Water and salt
easy.explanation: The verse forbids bringing the hire of a whore or the price of a dog into the house of the LORD.

easy.question: For what purpose might someone try to bring the money into the house of the LORD?
answers: For any vow
To buy clothing
To pay a tax
easy.explanation: The verse mentions bringing such money for a vow, but forbids doing so.

medium.question: What is the connection between verses 18 and 19?
answers: Both prohibit things associated with prostitution and improper cultic practice
Both concern only gifts to the poor
The second verse cancels the first
medium.explanation: The first verse prohibits cultic prostitution, and the second prohibits bringing its earnings or the price of a dog into the LORD's house.

medium.question: In the phrase “the hire of a whore,” what does “hire” mean?
answers: A special garment
Payment or wages given to a prostitute
A gift to a poor person
medium.explanation: The context makes clear that “hire” means payment received for prostitution.

medium.question: Why is the money forbidden even if it is intended for a vow?
answers: Because its source is considered an abomination
Because no money may ever be brought to the LORD's house
Because every vow is forbidden
medium.explanation: The prohibition is based on the money's abominable source, not on a general ban against money or vows.

challenge.question: What precise conclusion follows about money from the hire of a prostitute or the price of a dog?
answers: It cannot be made acceptable for the LORD's house merely by assigning it to a vow
It is permitted if the amount is small
It is permitted if the priest agrees
challenge.explanation: The verse expressly includes money intended for any vow, so a good purpose does not change its forbidden source.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by “even both these”?
answers: Only the hire of a prostitute is forbidden
Both things mentioned are considered abominations
Only the price of a dog is forbidden
challenge.explanation: The expression emphasizes that both the prostitute's hire and the dog's price are included in the prohibition.

challenge.question: What detail shows that the prohibition in verse 18 includes both women and men?
answers: The word “house”
The word “vow”
The phrases “daughters of Israel” and “sons of Israel”
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly mentions both Israel's daughters and Israel's sons.

questions.question: What precise conclusion follows about money from the hire of a prostitute or the price of a dog?
answers: It cannot be made acceptable for the LORD's house merely by assigning it to a vow
It is permitted if the amount is small
It is permitted if the priest agrees
questions.explanation: The verse expressly includes money intended for any vow, so a good purpose does not change its forbidden source.

questions.question: What is emphasized by “even both these”?
answers: Only the hire of a prostitute is forbidden
Both things mentioned are considered abominations
Only the price of a dog is forbidden
questions.explanation: The expression emphasizes that both the prostitute's hire and the dog's price are included in the prohibition.

questions.question: What detail shows that the prohibition in verse 18 includes both women and men?
answers: The word “house”
The word “vow”
The phrases “daughters of Israel” and “sons of Israel”
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly mentions both Israel's daughters and Israel's sons.

paragraphs.title: Lending Without Interest to a Brother

easy.question: From whom is it forbidden to take interest according to the verses?
answers: From your brother
From a stranger only
From every person without exception
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thou shalt not lend upon usury to thy brother.”

easy.question: What forms of interest are mentioned in the verse?
answers: Money only
Money, food, and anything else that is lent
Food only
easy.explanation: The verse mentions interest on money, food, and anything else that is lent.

easy.question: What blessing is connected with obeying the command?
answers: The person will become rich immediately
He will not have to work
The LORD will bless him in everything he does
easy.explanation: The verse promises that the LORD will bless him in all that he sets his hand to.

medium.question: Why does the Torah distinguish between a brother and a stranger concerning interest?
answers: Economic dealings within Israel should express mutual help and brotherhood
Trade with strangers is forbidden
A brother may not borrow money
medium.explanation: The prohibition toward one's brother emphasizes responsibility and assistance within the community.

medium.question: In the phrase “unto a stranger thou mayest lend upon usury,” what does “lend upon usury” mean?
answers: Charge interest on a loan
Give a gift without repayment
Demand the money immediately
medium.explanation: In this financial context, it means charging interest on a loan.

medium.question: What cause-and-effect relationship appears in the verse?
answers: If he lends money, he cannot inherit the land
If he avoids charging interest to his brother, the LORD may bless his work
If he charges a stranger interest, he will not need to work
medium.explanation: “That the LORD thy God may bless thee” presents blessing as connected with obeying the command.

challenge.question: What detail in the verses is easy to miss?
answers: The verse also includes “anything else,” not only money and food
The verse forbids only loans of food
The verse concerns only trade in the land
challenge.explanation: After mentioning money and food, the verse adds anything else that may be lent, broadening the wording.

challenge.question: What central contrast is created in the second verse?
answers: Work and rest
Treatment of a stranger and treatment of one's brother
Money and food
challenge.explanation: The verse contrasts lending upon interest to a stranger with not doing so to one's brother.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the ending, “in the land whither thou goest to possess it”?
answers: The command concerns the people entering the land and building their lives there
The command applies only during war
The command is intended only for those outside the land
challenge.explanation: The ending connects economic conduct and blessing with life in the land Israel is about to possess.

questions.question: What detail in the verses is easy to miss?
answers: The verse also includes “anything else,” not only money and food
The verse forbids only loans of food
The verse concerns only trade in the land
questions.explanation: After mentioning money and food, the verse adds anything else that may be lent, broadening the wording.

questions.question: What central contrast is created in the second verse?
answers: Work and rest
Treatment of a stranger and treatment of one's brother
Money and food
questions.explanation: The verse contrasts lending upon interest to a stranger with not doing so to one's brother.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the ending, “in the land whither thou goest to possess it”?
answers: The command concerns the people entering the land and building their lives there
The command applies only during war
The command is intended only for those outside the land
questions.explanation: The ending connects economic conduct and blessing with life in the land Israel is about to possess.

paragraphs.title: Keeping Vows and Fulfilling One's Word

easy.question: What must a person do after making a vow to the LORD?
answers: Fulfill it on time
Forget the vow
Replace the vow
easy.explanation: The verse commands that the vow not be delayed but be paid.

easy.question: What is said about a person who chooses not to make a vow?
answers: He must make one immediately
There is no sin in him
He must bring an offering
easy.explanation: The verse says, “If thou shalt forbear to vow, it shall be no sin in thee.”

easy.question: What must a person do with what has come from his mouth?
answers: Hide it
Tell it only to others
Keep and perform what he vowed
easy.explanation: The verse says, “That which is gone out of thy lips thou shalt keep and perform.”

medium.question: Why must fulfillment of a vow not be delayed?
answers: Because the LORD requires it, and delay may be sinful
Because every vow must be canceled
Because speaking with people is forbidden
medium.explanation: The verse says that the LORD will require the vow, and failing to fulfill it is a sin.

medium.question: What does “forbear” mean in “if thou shalt forbear to vow”?
answers: Begin
Refrain or abstain
Hurry
medium.explanation: “Forbear” means to refrain; the verse refers to choosing not to make a vow.

medium.question: What sequence is described in verse 24?
answers: Making vows, forgetting them, and canceling them
Speaking, regretting, and waiting
Making a vow, keeping one's word, and fulfilling it
medium.explanation: A person first makes a vow, then must keep his word and do what he promised.

challenge.question: What distinction emerges from comparing verses 22–23?
answers: There is no obligation to vow, but once a person vows, he must fulfill it
There is an obligation to vow but not to fulfill it
Both making and fulfilling vows are forbidden
challenge.explanation: Verse 23 says there is no sin in refraining from a vow, while verse 22 requires a person who vows to fulfill it.

challenge.question: What does “thy lips” emphasize in “that which is gone out of thy lips”?
answers: Private thoughts only
Words spoken aloud by the person
Words spoken by other people
challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes that the vow was spoken, creating responsibility for the words one uttered.

challenge.question: What does the repetition in “the LORD will surely require it” suggest?
answers: The vow is unimportant
A person may postpone it indefinitely
The LORD takes the vow seriously and holds the person accountable
challenge.explanation: The repeated wording emphasizes the seriousness of the vow and the duty to fulfill it.

paragraphs.title: Eating from Another's Field Within Proper Limits

easy.question: What may a person do when entering his neighbor's vineyard?
answers: Eat grapes
Take all the grapes
Sell the grapes
easy.explanation: The verse permits eating grapes in a neighbor's vineyard.

easy.question: What may not be used when eating in the vineyard?
answers: Hands
A container
Eyes
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thou shalt not put any in thy vessel.”

easy.question: What may a person do in his neighbor's standing corn?
answers: Harvest the whole field
Set the field on fire
Pluck the ears with his hand
easy.explanation: The verse permits plucking ears by hand but forbids harvesting with a sickle.

medium.question: What is the main difference between the rule for the vineyard and the rule for the standing corn?
answers: In the vineyard one may eat grapes, while in the standing corn one may pluck by hand
One may not enter a vineyard, but may enter a field
One may use a tool in the vineyard but may not eat in the field
medium.explanation: In the vineyard one may eat grapes without collecting them in a container; in the field one may pluck a small amount by hand.

medium.question: What does “at thine own pleasure” mean in “thou mayest eat grapes thy fill at thine own pleasure”?
answers: Secretly
As much as you wish, to satisfy your hunger
Only one grape
medium.explanation: The phrase permits eating according to one's desire and until satisfied.

medium.question: Why is it forbidden to use a sickle on one's neighbor's standing corn?
answers: So a person will not harvest his neighbor's crop as if it were his own
So he cannot enter the field
So he will not eat too many grapes
medium.explanation: A sickle would allow someone to take a large amount instead of merely plucking a little by hand.

challenge.question: What action is permitted in both verses?
answers: Collecting grain in a sack
Eating or plucking by hand instead of gathering a large amount
Harvesting the neighbor's field with a sickle
challenge.explanation: Both passages allow taking a small amount for immediate eating but forbid large-scale gathering or harvesting.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the difference between a “vessel” and a “sickle”?
answers: The Torah forbids only entering a field
The Torah distinguishes personal eating from broad or commercial harvesting
The Torah permits taking the entire crop without limit
challenge.explanation: A vessel and a sickle are means of collecting or harvesting a large amount, so only eating or hand-plucking is permitted.

challenge.question: What wording emphasizes that the permission in the vineyard is for eating there, not for collecting?
answers: “Thou shalt not put any in thy vessel”
“Thy neighbour's standing corn”
“When thou comest”
challenge.explanation: The prohibition against putting grapes in a container makes clear that a person may eat but may not gather them for himself.
